speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing those details. Has there been any change in his personality, such as increased apathy or irritability, and has he experienced any episodes of confusion or disorientation?

speaker: Doctor
text: Has he experienced any headaches, visual changes, or seizures, and has there been any decline in his ability to perform complex tasks like managing finances? I also need to know if he has any history of head trauma or alcohol abuse.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will request a brain MRI to look for frontal lobe atrophy, which is highly suggestive of Frontotemporal Dementia given the behavioral changes and hyperphagia. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected given the classic behavioral presentation. I need to rule out other metabolic or infectious causes for these symptoms. Does the patient have any history of syphilis, HIV, or vitamin B12 deficiency, and has he experienced any tremors or motor disturbances?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient avoids questions and instead comments on unrelated subjects. Shows apathy towards surroundings and interactions.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI is puzzling, but the clinical picture of disinhibition, hyperphagia, and apathy remains classic for behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia, which can sometimes present with subtle or delayed imaging findings. To further evaluate cognitive decline and rule out other dementias, I will order a comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation. REQUEST TEST: Neuropsychological_Evaluation

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal neuropsychological evaluation is highly unusual for FTD given the severe behavioral symptoms. I need to rule out a frontal lobe lesion that might be missed on standard MRI, so I will request a PET scan to assess glucose metabolism in the frontal and temporal lobes. REQUEST TEST: Brain_PET_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal PET scan effectively rules out neurodegenerative dementia like FTD, pointing strongly toward a psychiatric disorder such as Bipolar Disorder or Schizophrenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Bipolar Disorder
